ASAD-NOTES:7:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:intro/r3.claim: Human weakness and susceptibility to appetite, vanity, and false self-interest make continuing prophetic guidance necessary; Adam and Eve's fall and Iblis's temptation illustrate this condition.
ASAD-NOTES:7:intro/r3.anchor: The need for continued prophetic guidance arises from the fact of man's weakness

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.claim: Verses 11–27 recount Adam's creation, temptation, and expulsion from the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.anchor:
the story of Adam’s creation, temptation, and exile from
the Garden.

TABATABAI:7:34-35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:34-35/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:34-35/r2.claim: He suggests 7:25 concerns the life and death of each person and community within humanity’s larger lifespan, while the earlier earthly provision lasts until humanity’s extinction or resurrection.
TABATABAI:7:34-35/r2.anchor: راجع إلى حياة النوع إلى حين وهو حين الانقراض أو البعث

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.claim: The statement about living, dying, and being raised on earth depicts humanity’s earthly phases before God shows people what they gained or lost and whether they won.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p19/.anchor: after they return, they would be informed by God what they gained and lost and if they won or lost.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r85.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r85.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r85.claim: The sequence of earthly life, death, and resurrection reminds people of their ultimate fate.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r85.anchor: a reminder of which is provided by the reference to earthly life, earthly death, and resurrection (being brought forth) in v. 25.

SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r1.speaker: الأخوان وابن ذكوان
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r1.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Dhakwān read actively here and at 45:35, 43:11, and 30:19; Ibn Dhakwān differs in the first occurrence at 30:19.
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r1.anchor: قرأ الأخوان وابن ذكوان " تخرجون " هنا، وفي الجاثية

SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r2.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r2.claim: The remaining readers use the passive; both readings are clear.
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r2.anchor: والباقون قرؤوه مبنيا للمفعول، وفي أول الروم خلاف عن ابن ذكوان

SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r3.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r3.claim: In the prayer at 30:23, omitting يا exalts God; since the vocative carries an imperative-like sense, its omission removes that force.
SAMIN-DURR:7:25/r3.anchor: قال مكي: " ونداء الرب قد كثر حذف " يا " منه في القرآن

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وعاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r1.claim: They read تُخرجون with passive ḍamma on tāʾ and fatḥa on rāʾ here and in the cited forms at al-Rūm, al-Zukhruf, and al-Jāthiya; the readings of two other cited forms open the initial letter.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو، ونافع، وعاصم ومنها تخرجون، بضم التاء وفتح الراء

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r2.claim: They read تُخرجون actively, with fatḥa on tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ; they use the corresponding forms at al-Rūm, al-Zukhruf, and al-Jāthiya.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: ومنها تخرجون في الأعراف، بفتح التاء وضم الراء

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir opens tāʾ only in this verse and uses ḍamma in the corresponding readings elsewhere.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r3.anchor: وفتح ابن عامر التاء في الأعراف فقط

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r4.claim: The passive reading is supported by the expression مخرجون and by the verse saying that God brings the dead forth; these parallel the sense of being brought out.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r5.claim: The active reading is supported by the agreed active form إذا أنتم تخرجون, by the people themselves being the grammatical subject in ينسلون, and by the surrounding sequence and return imagery.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p9/r5.anchor: وحجة من قال: (تخرجون) اتفاق الجميع في قوله: ثم إذا دعاكم

NASHR:v2p267/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p267/r1.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وخلف
NASHR:v2p267/r1.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf use fatḥ on the imperfect prefix and ḍamm on rāʾ in all four cited places; Yaʿqūb and Ibn Dhakwān agree at 7:25, and Ibn Dhakwān also agrees in al-Zukhruf.
NASHR:v2p267/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بفتح حرف المضارعة وضم الراء في الأربعة، وافقهم يعقوب وابن ذكوان هنا

QIRAAT-ER:7:25:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:25:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:25:9#1/r1.claim: The active reading means you yourselves come out rather than you are brought out, shifting agency from divine extraction to autonomous emergence.
QIRAAT-ER:7:25:9#1/r1.anchor: Shifts agency from divine extraction to autonomous emergence. Canonical in 7 reading traditions.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r8.claim: This explains the earthly settlement and provision mentioned in 7:24: life there lasts until death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r8.anchor: هذا كالتفسير لقوله ولكم في الأرض مستقر ومتاع إلى حين أي بالحياة إلى حين الموت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r9.claim: قال lacks a conjunction because this sentence explains the preceding one; Arabic usually coordinates successive sentences unless the latter interprets the former.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r9.anchor: ولذلك جاء قال بغير واو العطف إذ الأكثر في لسان العرب إذا لم تكن الجملة تفسيرية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r10.claim: The final phrase alerts people to resurrection and their emergence for recompense in reward or punishment, like 20:55.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r10.anchor: وتمم هنا المقصود بالتنبيه على البعث والنشور بقوله ومنها تخرجون أي إلى المجازاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r11.speaker: الأخوان وابن ذكوان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r11.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī, together with Ibn Dhakwān, read تخرجون in the active voice here and in the cited passages; Ibn Dhakwān differs on the opening of al-Rūm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r11.anchor: وقرأ الأخوان وابن ذكوان تخرجون مبنيا للفاعل هنا وفي الجاثية والزخرف وأول الروم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r12.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p28#2/r12.claim: The other readers among the Seven read تخرجون in the passive voice.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r1.claim: The renewed ‘He said’ marks a fresh utterance or emphasizes what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r1.anchor: أعيد للاستئناف إما للايذان بعدم اتصال ما بعده بما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r2.claim: Humanity lives and dies on earth and is brought out from it at the resurrection on Judgment Day.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r3.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r3.claim: The Kūfan readers except ʿĀṣim read with fatḥa on tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ, as an active construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p103/r3.anchor: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم ( تخرجون ) بفتح التاء وضم الراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p221/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p221/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p221/r1.claim: People live on the earth, die there, and are raised from its graves for resurrection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p221/r1.anchor: {قال فيها تحيون} يعني في الأرض تعيشون، {وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p221/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p221/r2.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p221/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, and al-Kisaʾi read with ta fatḥa here and in 43:11; Yaʿqub agrees here, and Hamza and al-Kisaʾi also use that reading in 30:19; the rest use ta damma and ra fatḥa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p221/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: {تخرجون} بفتح التاء هاهنا وفي الزخرف، وافق يعقوب هاهنا وزاد حمزة والكسائي: "وكذلك تخرجون" في أول الروم،

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:25/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:25/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:25/r1.claim: People live and die on earth and are brought out of it for judgment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:25/r1.anchor: ومنها تخرجون } للجزاء وقرأ حمزة والكسائي

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:25/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:25/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وابن ذكوان
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:25/r2.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Dhakwān read the phrase with fatḥa on tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ, an active form; the same reading occurs in 43:11.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:25/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وابن ذكوان { ومنها تخرجون } ، وفي

BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r1.speaker: الفلاسفة التناسخية
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r1.claim: Biqaʿi rejects the view of transmigrationist philosophers who say souls leave bodies at death for celestial beings or realms and have no further bodily attachment or resurrection.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r1.anchor: من الفلاسفة التناسخية وغيرهم ممن يقر بالوحدانية من يقول

BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r2.claim: Human beings live in this earth first and again, in both outward and inward life as bodies and souls; the verse excludes another earthly realm.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r2.anchor: أي أولا وثانيا على ما أنتم عليه بظواهركم وبواطنكم ابدانا وأرواحا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r3.claim: People die in this earth as a whole, yet souls retain some connection to bodies, allowing the dead to answer the angels in the grave and bodies to feel pleasure or pain.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r3.anchor: أي من الحياة الأولى بجملتكم فيكون للارواح تعلق بالأبدان بوجه ما

BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r4.claim: The dead emerge from this earth as body and soul after returning to dust, to be requited and to manifest God's justice by restoring rights among people.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r4.anchor: أي روحا وبدنا بعد موتكم فيها وعودكم إلى ما كنتم عليه أولا ترابا

BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p18/r5.claim: The affirmation of resurrection concludes the story by returning to the afterlife message with which it began.

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r6.claim: People live and are buried in the earth, then emerge from it for requital; Adam inferred that he would return to Paradise and was comforted by God's promise.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r6.anchor: {قال} الله تعالى {فيها تحيون} أي : في الأرض تعيشون {وفيها تموتون} وتقبرون

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r7.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r7.claim: Al-Qushayrī depicts Adam as once honored above creation, then stripped of his garments and ease after one sin; this warns how much worse many sins may be for us.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r7.anchor: قال الإمام القشيري : ونعم ما قال : أصبح آدم عليه السلام محسود الملائكة

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r8.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r8.claim: Ḥāfiẓ's couplet laments longing for union while one's soul remains bound by destiny to separation.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r8.anchor: قال الحافظ : ه كونه دعوىء وصلت كنم بجانكه شدست

BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r9.claim: Divine decree governs everyone, whether prophet or saint.
BURSEVI:v3p111#4/r9.anchor: وقضاء الله تعالى يجري على كل أحد نبيا كان أو وليا

BURSEVI:v3p112/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p112/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p112/r1.claim: In the inward reading, living there means love, sincere seeking, patient endurance, and steadfast servitude while awaiting relief.
BURSEVI:v3p112/r1.anchor: قال تعالى : {فيها تحيون} أي : في المحبة وصدق الطلب

BURSEVI:v3p112/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p112/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p112/r2.claim: Dying there means seeking the Real on the path of the Sharīʿa through the discipline of the ṭarīqa; emerging is arrival in the realm of reality.

BURSEVI:v3p112/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p112/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v3p112/r3.claim: A Prophetic report says that as people live, they die, and as they die, they are raised.
BURSEVI:v3p112/r3.anchor: كما تعيشون تموتون وكما تموتون تبعثون

BURSEVI:v3p112/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p112/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p112/r4.claim: The Persian verses urge striving for love and say that night prayer and dawn weeping guided the speaker through darkness.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r1.claim: Repeating قال without a conjunction departs from the expected coordination, although the speaker and general purpose are the same.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r1.anchor: والغرضض متحدا ، خروجا عن مقتضى الظاهر لأن مقتضى الظاهر في مثله هو العطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r2.speaker: جمهور الحذاق من المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur says most leading commentators did not explain the lack of coordination, perhaps treating it as a storytelling convention; al-Zamakhshari is among them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r2.anchor: وقد أهمل توجيه ترك العطف جمهور الحذاق من المفسرين : الزمخشري وغيره ، ولعله رأى ذلك أسلوبا من أساليب الحكاية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r3.speaker: ابن عرفة التونسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r3.claim: Ibn Arafa explains the analogous repeated قال at 7:140 by a change in discourse: the first statement rejects idolatry itself, the second argues against it; al-Khafaji also gives this explanation without attribution.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r3.anchor: هو الشيخ محمد بن عرفة التونسي في ( املاءات التفسير ) المروية عنه ، فإنه قال في قوله تعالى الآتي في هذه السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r4.speaker: أبو السعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r4.claim: Abu al-Su'ud offers as one explanation that repeating قال emphasizes the statement that they will live on earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r4.anchor: وقال أبو السعود : إعادة القول إما لإظهار الاعتناء بمضمون ما بعده ، وهو قوله : { فيها تحيون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r5.speaker: أبو السعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r5.claim: Abu al-Su'ud also suggests omitted intervening speech, comparing 15:56–57 and 17:61–62; Ibn Ashur rejects this because reported speech need not be exhaustive or continuous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p69#3/r5.anchor: والتوجيه الثاني مردود إذ لا يلزم في حكاية الأقوال الإحاطة ولا الاتصال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r9.claim: This is an irrevocable divine decree: people live and die on earth, then are raised from it alive for the gathering, as God will restore the first creation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r9.anchor: حكم من الله عز وجل أمضاه وجعله حتما في رقاب العباد يحيون في الأرض ويموتون فيها ويبعثون منها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r10.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r10.claim: These readers use passive tukhrajūn with tāʾ in the ḍamma and rāʾ in the fatḥa here, and similarly in 30:19 and repeated occurrences, with the stated exceptions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو «تخرجون» بضم التاء وفتح الراء هنا، وفي الروم وكذلك تخرجون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r11.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r11.claim: The other two exceptions are 30:25 and 70:43, where the tāʾ or yāʾ is fatḥa and the rāʾ is ḍamma; the source says readers do not differ on them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r11.anchor: إلا في الروم إذا أنتم تخرجون [الآية: 25] وفي سأل سائل يوم يخرجون [الآية: 43] فإن هذين بفتح التاء والياء وضم الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r12.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read the form in 7:25 with fatḥa on tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r12.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي في الأعراف ومنها تخرجون [الآية: 25] بفتح التاء وضم الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r13.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r13.claim: Ibn Amir reads with fatḥa on tāʾ in al-Aʿraf and with ḍamma there in the remaining cases.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p388/r13.anchor: وفتح ابن عامر التاء في الأعراف وضمها في الباقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r1.claim: The pronoun in fiha refers to the earth: there you will live.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r1.anchor: ﴿ قال فيها تحيون ﴾ يعني الأرض واختلف القراء في تاء تخرجون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r2.speaker: ابن كثير، عاصم، أبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r2.claim: These readers use a ḍamma on the ta and fatḥa on the ra here and at the cited places in 30:19, 43:11, and 45:35.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو بضم التاء وفتح الراء هاهنا وفي الروم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r3.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi use fatḥa on the ta and ḍamma on the ra at the cited locations.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r3.anchor: وقرأهن حمزة والكسائي بفتح التاء وضم الراء وفتح ابن عامر التاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAmir opens the ta only in al-Aʿraf; in 30:25 and 70:43 the ta is open by consensus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p181/r4.anchor: وفتح ابن عامر التاء في الاعراف فقط فأما التي في الروم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399#2/r1.claim: Earth is humanity’s home during worldly life: people live and die there, lie buried in it, and are raised from it for Judgment, when God gathers the first and last and repays each for their deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p399#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى أنه يجعل (4) الأرض دارا لبني آدم مدة الحياة الدنيا، فيها محياهم وفيها مماتهم

JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the verb with fatḥa on tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ here and in 30:25 and 43:11; at 45:35 they also open yāʾ.
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي تخرجون بفتح التاء وضم الراء وكذلك في (الروم) وفي (الزخرف)

JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads with fatḥa on yāʾ here and in 43:11, but with passive vowels in 30:25 and 45:35.
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن [عامر] ههنا وفي (الزخرف) بفتح الياء

JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r3.speaker: يعقوب
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb reads with fatḥa on tāʾ here, but passive vowels on tāʾ and yāʾ in 30:25 and 43:11.
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب ههنا بفتح التاء وفي (الروم) و(الزخرف)

JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r4.claim: The active readings attribute the leaving to the people, while the passive readings leave the agent unnamed.
JISHUMI:v4p2523#2/r4.anchor: فالفتح على أن الخروج مضاف إليهم، والضم على ما لم يسم فاعله

MUQATIL:7:25/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:25/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:25/r1.claim: People live on earth and die there when their lifespans end; they will be brought out of it on the Day of Resurrection.
MUQATIL:7:25/r1.anchor: { قال فيها تحيون } ، يعني في الأرض، { وفيها تموتون } عند منتهى آجالكم، { ومنها تخرجون } [آية: 25] يوم القيامة.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p8/r1.claim: People live and die on earth, then are brought out for reward or punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p8/r1.anchor: ﴿ قال فيها تحيون ﴾ فى الأرض ﴿ وفيها تموتون ومنها تخرجون ﴾ للثواب والعقاب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p8/r2.speaker: حمزة وعلى
NASAFI-FULL:v2p8/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī transmit a variant reading of tukhrajūn.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:25/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:25/r1.claim: All pronouns refer to the earth; the verse's qala lacks a preceding wāw, though including one would also be grammatical, as in the cited example about Zayd speaking to Amr.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:25/r1.anchor: الضمائر كلها للأرض. ولم يذكر الواو في «قال»، ولو ذكرها لجاز أيضا. وهو كقولك: قال زيد لعمرو كذا قال له كذا.

RAZI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says this account, explained in al-Baqara, implies Adam committed a grave sin, but resolves the question by placing it before prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية مفسرة في سورة البقرة ، وقد ذكرنا هناك أن هذه الآية تدل على صدور الذنب العظيم من آدم عليه السلام

TAB-FULL:v10p119/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r1.claim: People live on earth throughout the days of their lives.
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r1.anchor: {فيها تحيون} [الأعراف: 25] يقول: في الأرض تحيون، يقول: تكونون فيها أيام حياتكم

TAB-FULL:v10p119/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r2.claim: People die on earth; it is the place of their death.
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r2.anchor: {وفيها تموتون} [الأعراف: 25] ، يقول: في الأرض تكون وفاتكم

TAB-FULL:v10p119/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r3.claim: God brings people out of the earth and gathers them alive for resurrection on the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v10p119/r3.anchor: ومن الأرض يخرجكم ربكم، ويحشركم إليه لبعث القيامة أحياء

SULAMI:v1p225/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p225/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p225/r1.claim: In earthly life one lives through gnosis and dies through ignorance; emergence leads into prior decrees and the judgments that govern people.
SULAMI:v1p225/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : فيها تحيون بالمعرفة ، وفيها تموتون بالجهل ، ومنها تخرجون بما أنتم فيه من التقدير والتدبير

TABRISI:7:22-25/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:22-25/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:22-25/r15.claim: People live and die on earth and will be raised from it at the resurrection.
TABRISI:7:22-25/r15.anchor: عند البعث يوم القيامة قال الجبائي:

TABRISI:7:22-25/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:22-25/r16.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:7:22-25/r16.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī argues that resurrection is from this same earth; afterward God destroys it and moves people by a blast to another earth called al-Sāhira, citing 79:14.
TABRISI:7:22-25/r16.anchor: قال الجبائي: في الآية دلالة على أن الله سبحانه يخرج العباد يوم القيامة

TABRISI:7:22-25#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:22-25#2/r1.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:7:22-25#2/r1.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī cites 79:14 for his account that the resurrected are moved to the land called al-Sāhira.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the earth in which people live as the earth of this world.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: الأرض أرض الدنيا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi says the pronoun returns to the preceding statement that people have an abode on earth in 7:24.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r2.anchor: والكناية عائدة إلى قوله: {ولكم في الأرض مستقر}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi explains that people live and are buried in the earth, then emerge from their graves from the earth for resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p72#2/r3.anchor: في الأرض تعيشون، وفي الأرض قبوركم، ومن الأرض تخرجون من قبوركم للبعث

ELMALILI:7:23-25/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:23-25/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:23-25/r7.claim: On earth humanity will live and die, then be brought out for resurrection; God has thus established the human species on earth.
ELMALILI:7:23-25/r7.anchor: ve yine ondan çıkarılacaksınız, ba‘s ü neşr olunacaksınız

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r2.claim: Humanity was ordained to spread and settle on earth, live and die there, and be resurrected from it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r2.anchor: insan soyunun yeryüzüne dağılıp orada karar kılmaları ve barınmaları, orada yaşayıp orada ölmeleri, yeniden orada dirilmeleri takdir edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9.claim: The move from first sin and expulsion marks humanity’s moral rise into a free, accountable kind of being able to err, repent, and consciously choose goodness, not a moral decline.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:24/r9.anchor: ilk günahla başlayan ve cennetten çıkarılma ile devam eden süreç, insanlık için ahlâkî bakımdan bir düşüşü değil, bir yükselişi

BURHAN:v3p243/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p243/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p243/r1.claim: If death is nonbeing, its relation to life is privation and possession, though the sounder account calls them contraries.
BURHAN:v3p243/r1.anchor: فإن قلنا عدمي فالتقابل بينه وبين الحياة تقابل العدم والملكة وعلى الصحيح تقابل التضاد

BURHAN:v3p243/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p243/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p243/r2.claim: Death may precede because it is prior as nonexistence, or because life's departure is the final destination toward which worldly life moves; the ordering can also disparage the transient world and direct desire beyond death.
BURHAN:v3p243/r2.anchor: أو معدوم الحياة الذي هو مفارقة الروح البدني يجوز أن يكون لكونه الغاية التي يساق إليها في دار الدنيا

BURHAN:v3p243/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p243/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p243/r3.claim: Life precedes death if the address concerns Adam and Eve because they lived before dying, or if it addresses people who are alive before their eventual death.
BURHAN:v3p243/r3.anchor: إن كان الخطاب لآدم وحواء فلأن حياتهما في الدنيا سبقت الموت وإن كان للخلق بالخطاب لمن هو حي يعقبه الموت

BURHAN:v3p243/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p243/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p243/r9.claim: The author asks why life precedes death in the verse and also raises the contrary sequence in the command to Mary, whose answer lies beyond this excerpt.
BURHAN:v3p243/r9.anchor: فإن قيل فما وجه تقدم الحياة في قوله

TABATABAI:7:20-25/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r9.claim: This decree ties them to earth until resurrection; the address probably includes Adam, his wife, and their descendants, as a new “He said” introduces it.
TABATABAI:7:20-25/r9.anchor: قضاء آخر يوجب تعلقهم بالأرض إلى حين البعث

MAJAZ:v1p213/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p213/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p213/r1.claim: Riyāshan is the same as rīshan: visible clothing and adornment. It can mean clothing and equipment, including a saddle’s trappings, and also abundance or livelihood.
MAJAZ:v1p213/r1.anchor: «ورياشا» (25) [الرياش والريش واحد] ، وهو ما ظهر من اللباس والشارة وبعضهم يقول
